## Summary
Implement the HyDE context assembly step that generates a hypothetical document, retrieves from 4 sources (LOCAL lecture chunks, STRUCTURED KG paths, LOD briefs, GLOBAL reference), and merges via RRF (k=60) into a token-budgeted context window.

## User story
As a pipeline step, I need to assemble the richest possible context from multiple sources, so that the core generation step has enough grounded material to produce clinically accurate, curriculum-aligned items.

## Why this matters
Context quality directly determines item quality. Too little context produces hallucinated items. Too much context wastes tokens and money. The 4-source architecture ensures items are grounded in lecture material (LOCAL), knowledge graph structure (STRUCTURED), LOD briefs (LOD), and biomedical reference (GLOBAL). If HyDE fails, all downstream steps produce garbage.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Generates a hypothetical document (HyDE) from ECD output using HAIKU_MODEL
- [ ] Retrieves from 4 sources with token budgets: LOCAL 3000t, STRUCTURED 800t, LOD 500t, GLOBAL 400t
- [ ] LOCAL: MedCPT (768-dim) embedding similarity search against lecture ContentChunks
- [ ] STRUCTURED: Neo4j graph traversal paths from SubConcept hub
- [ ] LOD: SubConcept LOD briefs from Supabase `subconcept_lod_briefs` table (Rule 7)
- [ ] GLOBAL: text-embedding-3-small (1536-dim) search against HetioNet/DrugBank reference nodes
- [ ] RRF merge with k=60 for combining LOCAL + GLOBAL ranked results
- [ ] Total context window capped at 4700 tokens
- [ ] Graceful degradation: if any source fails, continue with remaining sources
- [ ] All content sanitized via sanitizeForContext before inclusion (Rule 5)
- [ ] Content wrapped in `<lecture_content>...</lecture_content>` XML delimiters (Rule 5)
- [ ] Promise.allSettled for parallel source retrieval (Rule 3)

## Canonical decisions in play
| Rule | What it means for this story |
|---|---|
| Rule 1 (C05) | neo4jQuery for STRUCTURED source (KG path traversal) |
| Rule 3 | Promise.allSettled for parallel 4-source retrieval |
| Rule 4 (D05) | HAIKU_MODEL for HyDE generation |
| Rule 5 (H12) | sanitizeForContext + buildContextBlock + XML delimiters for all retrieved content |
| Rule 7 (G05) | LOD briefs read from Supabase subconcept_lod_briefs, NOT Neo4j properties |
| Rule 12 (D04) | Retrieved chunks must be 150-250 tokens each |

## Code patterns to follow
```typescript
// apps/inngest/functions/p3-steps/hyde-context-assembly.ts
import { neo4jQuery } from '@journey/neo4j/client';
import { safeJsonParse } from '@journey/ai/safe-parse';
import { HAIKU_MODEL } from '@journey/ai/constants';
import { sanitizeForContext, buildContextBlock } from '@journey/ai/sanitize';

const TOKEN_BUDGETS = {
  LOCAL: 3000,
  STRUCTURED: 800,
  LOD: 500,
  GLOBAL: 400,
} as const;

export async function hydeContextAssembly(ecdOutput: ECDOutput, specData: SpecData) {
  // Step 1: Generate hypothetical document via Haiku
  const hydeDoc = await generateHyDE(ecdOutput, specData);

  // Step 2: Retrieve from 4 sources in parallel (Promise.allSettled!)
  const [localResult, structuredResult, lodResult, globalResult] =
    await Promise.allSettled([
      retrieveLocal(hydeDoc, TOKEN_BUDGETS.LOCAL),
      retrieveStructured(ecdOutput.proficiencyVars, TOKEN_BUDGETS.STRUCTURED),
      retrieveLOD(specData.subconcept_ids, TOKEN_BUDGETS.LOD),
      retrieveGlobal(hydeDoc, TOKEN_BUDGETS.GLOBAL),
    ]);

  // Step 3: RRF merge for ranked results
  // Step 4: Sanitize and wrap in XML delimiters
  const sanitized = sanitizeForContext(mergedContext);
  return buildContextBlock('generation_context', sanitized);
}
```
